segments.title: 第60章 等你下課
segments.content:
Chapter 60: Waiting for You After Class

In the campus of the First Affiliated High School, three teaching blocks and the cafeteria stood in the center, with the administration building and library to the east.

To the west were the sports field and the outdoor basketball courts.

Ying Chanxi followed Li Luo down the stairs on the west side of the teaching block, crossed the school's asphalt road, and arrived at the sports field.

At this moment, the field was completely empty. The few white lamps that had been on during the military training were now all switched off.

Walking beside Li Luo, Ying Chanxi felt no fear in the face of the dim sports field, but rather a faint sense of anticipation.

"Where are we going?" Ying Chanxi asked.

"Right here is fine." Li Luo walked over to the side of the flagpole platform, took out his guitar, and sat down on the steps.

While Li Luo was getting settled and casually strumming the strings, Ying Chanxi sat down next to him and turned her head to look at his somewhat serious profile.

"What are you planning to sing?"

"What do you want to hear?"

"Are there any songs about classmates or school life?"

"Let me think."

Li Luo lowered his head and began to play gently. A soothing rhythm flowed out, followed by his voice:

"Tomorrow, will you remember~"

"The diary you wrote yesterday~"

"Tomorrow, will you still think about~"

"The you who used to cry the most~"

Ying Chanxi knew at once that this song was "My Deskmate." Judging by the title, it was quite fitting for the occasion.

Because the two of them had been deskmates for a while in middle school.

"Who married the melancholic you~"

"Who read your diary~"

"Who tied up your long hair~"

"Who made your wedding dress~"

Hearing this part, Ying Chanxi started to dislike it a little.

But she just turned her head to look at Li Luo, and seeing him immersed in his singing, she couldn't bear to interrupt.

The song slowly came to an end. Li Luo turned to look at Ying Chanxi and asked with a smile, "How was it? Are you satisfied?"

"It was nice," Ying Chanxi nodded, then shook her head, "but this song is too sentimental. Do you have anything more upbeat?"

"Sure." Li Luo blinked, thought for a moment, and slowly began to strum the strings. "Then let's go with this one."

With the light music following the rhythm, Li Luo began to sing slowly: "In the alley where you live~"

"I rented an apartment~"

"Hoping to run into you by chance~"

Listening to the lyrics, Ying Chanxi couldn't help but raise an eyebrow, partly because she liked the content, and partly because she didn't think she had ever heard this song before.

"Lying on your school's sports field, gazing at the starry sky~"

"The lights in the classroom are still on, you haven't left~"

"Remembering~ the love letter I wrote to you~"

For some reason, Ying Chanxi felt her heart beating a little fast.

When Li Luo finished singing, she tucked a stray strand of hair behind her ear and asked in a low voice, "What song is this?"

"Waiting for You After Class."

"Is that the song title?" Ying Chanxi was a little curious and puzzled. "I don't think I've ever heard it before."

"This, uh..." Li Luo suddenly smiled a little shyly. "I had a dream before, and this song came to me in the dream."

"Huh?" Ying Chanxi was stunned for a moment, then it dawned on her. "So you wrote it yourself?"

"It was a dream transmission from Jay Chou."

"You're just talking nonsense." Ying Chanxi gave him a light smack, annoyed. "Then have him send you another song in a dream."

"I'll ask him next time I'm in a dream."

...

When he got home, Li Luo had just put on his slippers when he heard a sound from the kitchen.

He walked curiously to the kitchen doorway and glanced in, only to see Xu Youyu holding a kitchen knife, doing something unknown in front of the cutting board.

"Senior, are you cooking?" Li Luo asked in astonishment.

In his impression, Xu Youyu was a complete kitchen disaster. Hoping for her to cook a good meal was less realistic than hoping for her to write over ten thousand words a day.

Fortunately, Xu Youyu knew her own limitations. The moment she saw Li Luo return, she immediately ran out, grabbed his shoulders, and pushed him into the kitchen.

"Junior! You two are going to the military camp for training tomorrow. I think it's necessary to have a proper farewell meal to see you off!"

Xu Youyu said in all seriousness.

Li Luo was speechless. "...If you want to eat, just say so. No need to beat around the bush. It's not like I won't cook for you."

"I want some too," Ying Chanxi poked her head in and raised her hand. "Just a little is fine."

"Got it." Li Luo picked up the kitchen knife and tapped it on the cutting board. "Both of you, go out and wait."

Half an hour later, after a satisfying meal, Xu Youyu rubbed her belly and lay on the sofa without a care for her image, letting out a contented burp.

But the thought of Li Luo being gone tomorrow made her let out a gloomy sigh.

As the saying goes, the way to a woman's heart is through her stomach.

Xu Youyu felt like her stomach had been completely captured.

Just then, Ying Chanxi came out after a shower and sat down at the dining table to eat some fried rice. As she ate, she looked at Li Luo and said, "That new song you sang on the sports field today, could you sing it again?"

"Waiting for You After Class?"

"Yes, that's the one."

"Sure." Li Luo took out his guitar and sat on the sofa.

Xu Youyu, who was lying on the sofa, curled up her feet to make room and asked with a curious look on her face, "What new song?"

"A new song by Jay Chou," Li Luo spouted nonsense.

"What?" Xu Youyu was taken aback. "How come I didn't know he released a new song?"

As a web novel author who wrote about the entertainment industry, she naturally paid close attention to a king-tier singer like Jay Chou.

Xu Youyu quite enjoyed teasing future celebrities who weren't yet famous in her novels, occasionally bringing them out for a spin, which was always fun.

In her memory, there was indeed news that Jay Chou would be releasing a new album this year, but he definitely hadn't released anything recently. Where would a new song come from?

At that moment, Li Luo had already started singing.

Ying Chanxi ate her fried rice while listening to the song, her fair feet dangling and swinging under the table.

Xu Youyu also quickly became immersed in the song, momentarily forgetting to think.

Only after Li Luo finished singing did she come back to her senses and press him, "You didn't write this yourself, did you?"

"He said he dreamed it up," Ying Chanxi chuckled.

"Dream my ass." Xu Youyu rolled her eyes, then reminded him, "If you wrote it yourself, remember to register the copyright."

Xu Youyu's reminder made Li Luo suddenly realize something.

If he were to "plagiarize" some songs, could he also make some money?

A web novel's length of several million words was too much; reproducing it with his memory palace would be too mentally taxing.

But the mental load of recalling a single song wasn't that heavy.

But how does one make money from a song?

Take this same song, "Waiting for You After Class." Sung by Jay Chou versus sung by an unknown like himself, in the eyes of music companies, the prices would be worlds apart.

But there was no rush.

He was going to the military camp for training tomorrow. There wasn't enough time to record it and register the copyright.

For now, only Ying Chanxi and Xu Youyu had heard the song, so there was no need to worry about any copyright disputes.

"If you need help," Ying Chanxi thought for a moment, then said, "I can ask my dad for a favor. His company deals with film, television, and music."
